topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing for compliance
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-28
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Maya (AstraCommerce Head of ML), Liam (Platform), Priya (Finance), Ellen (Security)

[00:00] Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:06] Maya Patel (AstraCommerce): Yep, all good on our side. Thanks for coordinating.
[00:09] Liam O'Connor (AstraCommerce): Can hear you clearly.
[00:12] Sofia: Great. Agenda—run through where your usage has trended, go over capacity mapping and our suggested rightsizing, then cost model, and finish with security and next steps. Devon will take the deep perf bits. Sound good?
[00:23] Maya: Yep that's perfect.

[03:10] Devon Chen (Redwood SE): Cool. I'll start with a quick sketch of what we've observed from your tenant: peak RPS sits around 220 requests per minute during campaign windows, median payload length ~420 tokens, 95th percentile latency for hosted endpoints has been around 320 ms. There's a bimodal distribution—steady low-level traffic and short high-volume spikes tied to marketing emails.
[03:40] Priya Rao (AstraCommerce Finance): When you say 320 ms, that's per-request or per-token? Need that to map to cost.
[03:47] Devon: Good question—per-request end-to-end for the standard text generation endpoint, that includes network and model inference. Our internal per-token compute is around X but I'll attach the spreadsheet with the breakout.
[04:05] Maya: The spikes are the painful part. Right now we black-box scale in the app which doubles costs on a lot of nights. We're hoping to smooth that with queueing and some burst capacity.
[04:17] Ravi Kapoor (Redwood CSM): We suggested earlier a burst pool + autoscale policy—basically reserve baseline capacity for predictable steady state and consume burst credits for campaign spikes. That keeps unit cost lower across the month.

[06:30] Liam: For private deployment routing—if we move routing for HIPAA-ish traffic to our VPC, does the economics change materially? I.e., dedicated GPUs in private vs hosted endpoints.
[06:42] Devon: Dedicated/private will alter ops cost—you're paying for reserved capacity (VMs/GPUs) and network egress, but you'll get consistent p95 latency and higher throughput. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but can have noisier p95s during cloud-wide events. For AstraCommerce volumes, our model shows Dedicated becomes cheaper if sustained peak baseline above ~80 RPS for 30+ days; otherwise hosted with burst pools and smarter batching is preferable.
[07:10] Ellen Wu (AstraCommerce Security): Also we need to confirm KMS integration flow. Key control is non-negotiable for audit. Do you support customer-managed keys in the private plane?
[07:22] Sofia: Yes, private includes KMS/HSM integration. We'll send the flow diagram but short answer: customer-managed KMS is supported for Private; for Hosted we have envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys and optional bring-your-own-key for enterprise plans.

[09:00] Speaker 3: (unclear) I think we also saw a bunch of requests failing around last month during that deploy.
[09:06] Devon: Right—there was a configuration mismatch on route fallback; some requests retried and that spiked cost. We've patched the autoscaler triggers and added an alert for retry storms.
[09:20] Maya: Good to hear. Can you set a guardrail so that the app doesn't escalate to 4x capacity automatically?
[09:27] Ravi: Yes, we'll propose a policy—max burst multiplier and cool-down windows. We'll share policy templates.

[12:15] Devon: On batching and KV caching—your distribution shows a lot of repeated prefixes in customer messages. Enabling prefix KV caching on the inference path could cut tokens by ~12–18% for the most common flows. That also reduces compute and latency because we skip full-attention recompute for cached prefixes.
[12:40] Maya: Is that safe for our personalization flows? We use different user contexts.
[12:47] Devon: We can scope cache keys by user session or segment. The cache is configurable; if there's sensitive PII, we can exclude those flows. We'll prepare a config example.

[15:05] Priya: Walk me through the cost model again—what are the levers we control?
[15:12] Sofia: High level—batching (increases throughput, can slightly increase tail latency), quantization (saves compute), model choice (smaller model reduces cost but may affect quality), and routing (dedicated vs hosted and regional choice). Also KV caching and prefix reuse. We'll share updated cost-per-1M-token estimates in the sheet.
[15:40] Priya: Is there a simple way to understand break-even for dedicated vs hosted? Put a threshold.
[15:46] Devon: Yes—based on your numbers, break-even is roughly when average concurrent active inference sessions exceed 60–80 replicates sustained for the month. We'll give a concrete table with your specific token mix.

[18:50] Maya: On quality—we had a slight regression when you recommended quantized v2.1 for a subset. Can we do canary-based rollouts?
[18:58] Sofia: Absolutely. Our rollout supports canary by percentage, A/B with automatic rollback on quality regressions when tied to your eval set, and automatic fallback to a warm variant if latency balloons.
[19:12] Liam: How do we measure quality automatically? We have golden prompts but need a daily health metric.
[19:19] Devon: You can hook your prompt set into Redwood Optimize; we'll run daily evals and send regression alerts. We can also push a lightweight webhook with sample diffs.

[22:05] Ellen: Regarding audit logs, we require immutable request logs for 90 days with redaction markers. Can Redwood provide tamper-evident logs?
[22:15] Sofia: Yes—for enterprise we hold append-only logs with TTL controls and can integrate with your SIEM via S3/Cloud-connector. We'll include our logging architecture doc.

[25:00] Maya: About the benchmark—we want Redwood to run end-to-end with our staging dataset and realistic traffic. Scope: 3 model variants, two sequence lengths, with peak shaped load. Can you run and show p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens?
[25:13] Devon: That's exactly what we recommend. We'll provision a private benchmark run. We need your staging creds and a token distribution file.
[25:25] Maya: I'll send the token distribution and an obfuscated dataset—HIPAA-ized.

[28:40] Priya: For budget planning, can we model a 20% user growth next quarter and see resulting spend?
[28:47] Ravi: We'll run sensitivity analysis. Also we can show a rightsized reservation plan that smooths monthly spend with a reserved baseline and capped burst.
[29:05] Priya: Also include an option with 24/7 Dedicated baseline vs hosted plus burst credits.

[32:10] Devon: One more technical note—if you enable large batch sizes to lower unit compute, you might see higher p99 for single-user interactive flows. For chat-like interactions, we recommend adaptive batching: small batches for low-latency interactive sessions and large batches in background generation. Redwood supports that multiplexing.
[32:35] Liam: Is that automatic or do we need to instrument it?
[32:38] Devon: We can enable it at the route-level and we'll recommend heuristics based on session ids. We'll share suggested defaults.

[35:40] Maya: Security question—if we go private, where is the control plane hosted? We want the control plane in our region and data residency assurances.
[35:48] Sofia: Private includes a regional control plane option; the contract can specify region and egress controls. We'll note that in the security doc.
[36:05] Ellen: And backup keys—how frequently are they rotated and who has access?
[36:10] Sofia: Rotation is policy-driven; customer-managed keys mean your KMS rotation policy applies. For Redwood-managed, we rotate monthly and provide rotation proof in audit reports.

[39:20] Ravi: To recap the operational playbook we propose: 1) Reserved baseline for steady RPS, 2) Burst pool with capped multiplier and cool-down, 3) Enable KV prefix caching for eligible flows, 4) Benchmark run across 3 variants, 5) Security docs + KMS flow.
[39:45] Priya: Sounds good. What about contract amendments? I'd like burst pricing defined.
[39:50] Sofia: We'll draft an amendment with explicit burst credits, per-token price tiers, and an exit clause for overages.

[42:00] Maya: Any concerns about vendor lock if we heavily optimize for Redwood-specific caching?
[42:07] Devon: The cache policy is portable—keys are conceptually simple and we provide migration guidance. But yes, certain runtime optimizations are Redwood-specific so we'll include migration notes.

[44:30] Liam: Can you also show a sample app-level middleware we can drop in for adaptive batching?
[44:37] Devon: Yes—we'll push a Node and Python snippet.

[46:00] Sofia: Okay final wrap—I'll send the cost spreadsheet, the contract amendment draft, security docs and the benchmark request form. Can we confirm dates? Maya?
[46:09] Maya: We'll get token distribution to you by 11/02. Benchmark window week of 11/8 works. Ellen will review SOC2 artifacts on 10/30.
[46:20] Sofia: Great, thanks all.
[46:24] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript has occasional misattribution and short gaps typical of a remote call. Action items captured above.
